title: Китайские чаевые и заявление Феди  (Chinese Tips and Fedya's Notice)

segments.t: At the end of the exhausting Monday shift, Vika brings in a fat stack of tips left by the grateful Chinese tourists. Chef Barinov hands the reward to Max, who asks to share it equally with the whole crew, right before Fedya announces he is giving one month's notice.
Что все так сегодня замечательно получилось.

'Monday really is a heavy day.' Max brings out the contrast between 'Monday' and 'day' in a few short words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Well then.' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'what' in spoken Russian.
'Here are your Chinese tips.' Fedya brings out the contrast between 'there you go' and 'your' in a few short words.
'Come over here.' Max anchors the line on 'go', while 'here' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Take it, you earned this today.' In Russian, the idea of 'take' flows naturally into 'merit' without extra filler words.
'Chef, let us split it among all of us.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'chef' before landing on 'we'll divide'.
'I believe that is fair.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'consider' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.

'That everything turned out so wonderfully today.' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'worked out' in spoken Russian.

'But in a month I am leaving.' Notice how Russian expresses 'but' and 'will leave' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Consider this my official notice.' Fedya anchors the line on 'this', while 'warning' completes the thought.
'In one month.' In Russian, the idea of 'month' flows naturally into 'month' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
